questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I knew people who studied abroad in Edinburgh and they loved it. I also wanted to study in the UK, and this was one of the only places in the UK which still was a part of erasmus.

questions.answer: They sent mails to guide me through the process and were quite quick to answer my emails.

How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I started looking for accomodation for the fall semester in June. I used Spareroom and most people had not yet posted rooms available from September - so I could have waited for July or maybe even August. However, it did mean that I found a great room in the Meadowbank area so perhaps starting early was for the best. I was later also offered a room from the university but I declined it as it was very expensive compared to the room I had found.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You might have to take the bus more. If you are 21 or younger and stay in Edinburgh for more than 4 months (or is it 6?) you can apply for a Young Scots card. However, as I was only here for 3,5 months I had to pay for a ridacard which was very expensive. The good thing about living off campus is that you get to experience new parts of the city which are less touristy and busy (really loved this part).

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Apply for courses the moment you are able to. They fill up quickly.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I did two literature honours courses which were on a high level. The local students already knew a lot about the topics I was introduced to for the first time. However, with a bit of hard work it is very doable. I also did a first semester course on sociology which was easier.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very reminiscent of seminars at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Invitation to Sociology. Fiction and the Gothic. Novel and the Collapse of Humanism.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: As a literature student I really loved fiction and the gothic. My professor was great and the reading list was a dream.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I was a part of their knitting and crochet society. However, they had a lot of options.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I participated in a lot of the Erasmus+ activities in the beginning which was great for meeting people. The other people in the knitting society were also very friendly.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I booked a 3-day trip to the highlands which was wonderful (if a bit expensive). I also really loved Portobello Beach. And if you are under 25, you can see theatre performances at Capital Theatres for only 10 pounds!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I did not talk to many local students as many already had their own groups. However, I made a lot of friends with international students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really any

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The univeristy hosted Ceilidhs which were quite nice.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1. All of the Erasmus paperwork feels overwhelming, but worth it. 2. Try and participate in as much as you can in the welcome week but remember to take breaks as well. 3. The Law Library at Old College is way nicer than the Main Library.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really, sorry

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Learning a lot from my courses. Meeting so many nice people.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being away from friends and family.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
